sense: asking many people the same questions

terms.gloss: an inquiry, a questioning; a survey
evidence: Caes. B.G. 5.13.4: nōs nihil dē eō percontātiōnibus reperiēbāmus
terms.comment: Classically any asking around or close questioning; a survey by questionnaire is a modern thing, and the classical word covers it without a coinage. Also spelt percunctātiō; in rhetoric, a figure of speech (Cic. de Orat. 3.203).

terms.gloss: to ask around, to question, to inquire
terms.comment: To ask particularly, question closely (Lewis & Short); frequent in Plautus and in prose.

phrases.latin: Nōs nihil dē eō percontātiōnibus reperiēbāmus, nisi certīs ex aquā mēnsūrīs breviōrēs esse quam in continentī noctēs vidēbāmus.
phrases.english: We found out nothing about it by our inquiries, except that we saw from exact measurements by the water-clock that the nights were shorter than on the mainland.

sources: Lewis & Short: percontatio · Lewis & Short: percontor
